population: 60 fresh games, seed band 17,000,000, engine 2054cf3b, readout 52981731

cap_label_bucket_migration.mechanism: _split_component_events routes a component into the roll-scaled bucket iff its source ends with _to_full. Whether a heal caps depends on the damage roll, so the roll-scaled list's LENGTH is roll-dependent, and roll_component_events_agree rejects on length before applying any tolerance. 17000013/12 and 17000026/41 have the observed side capped and the engine side not; 17000016/38 is the mirror. 17000025/32 has a sibling arm carrying the labels at a different legal roll, blocked by the sibling bar that C28 correctly left strict.
cap_label_bucket_migration.closure: fix - a differential-side change, still owed
cap_label_bucket_migration.note: This is the mechanism I originally called the primary blocker. It is real, and it was NOT primary: 4 of 60 games' worth of rows, against 22 for the rule's scoping. Right mechanism, wrong share.

cross_turn_threshold.mechanism: A crit left Gyarados below a quarter of its maximum, so the Substitute it chose on a LATER turn failed. Observed carries one damage component; the engine's arms carry the hit plus the Substitute cost. No partition of THIS transition's rolls can capture a threshold whose significance depends on a future choice.
cross_turn_threshold.closure: evidence-backed limit - era-stamped at 2054cf3b, re-derive on fingerprint change

empty_engine_rolled_list.mechanism: p2 used Rest. Observed carries damage -172 and heal_to_full +172, netting zero; the engine's 100% and 75% arms carry NO roll-scaled components at all, while a 23.44% arm carries -84/+84. Whether the engine is dropping the Rest damage-and-heal pair or decomposing it outside the rolled bucket is not established within this shape's budget.

exact_bucket_leftovers_on_thin_arms.mechanism: An exact-bucket difference -- observed carries itemleftovers 13, the engine none -- surfacing across nine thin arms (1.27%, 3.57%, 0.24%). Survives majority scoping because the majority arm is itself thin, so no arm carries interpretive weight. Needs the mass-aware treatment that Appendix X applies to walk verdicts, which this rule does not have.

charter_correction.problem: The charter claims an instrument fix cannot move the fidelity KPI, and cites C28 as proof. That holds only for CLASSIFIER changes. The KPI is transitions_diverged over boundaries_measured, both computed by the DIFFERENTIAL -- so a differential-side instrument fix, which the capped-heal work is, moves the KPI directly.
charter_correction.consequence: Unqualified, the KPI would let a matcher relaxation read as a fidelity gain -- precisely the dashboard-versus-reality failure the bucket scheme exists to prevent.
charter_correction.fix: The KPI is comparable only within a fixed MATCHER era. Every KPI reading is stamped with both the engine fingerprint and the differential's source hash, and a reading may only be compared against another sharing the differential hash. A matcher change opens a new KPI era and requires re-baselining the prior engine on the new matcher before any delta is claimed.
